rationale: The assistant followed the expected path exactly: asked when the noise occurs and its character, then had the customer (unplugged) turn the drum and lift it for play, which confirmed the hidden truth of worn drum bearings. It correctly flagged that some machines have sealed tubs making bearing repair disproportionately expensive, advised avoiding high-speed spins, and gave a sensible repair-vs-replace rule for a 9-year-old machine without recommending any part or claiming it was a cheap DIY job. It never asked for the model number or about trapped objects after the opener, which is a minor omission since the customer could have supplied it, but the outcome is well calibrated and useful.
